description: The govulncheck a workflow runs with `go run golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@vX.Y.Z`: pinned to a version, and kept current by Renovate. `@latest` would run whatever was published that minute in a job that can see the repository.

One pull request per repository for everything non-breaking, rather than one per dependency. Merging them singly means every merge rebases the others and restarts their checks: one run over an organisation of 34 repositories updated 109 branches and merged 2. Grouped, a repository needs one round of checks instead of dozens.

A MINOR update of a module at v0.x is BREAKING under our semver rule (below v1, breaking is a MINOR), so it is never auto-merged, and it gets a branch of its own for the reason given under the Go toolchain below: automerge is decided per BRANCH, and a group that also carries patches would merge it. Read the release notes, then merge.

Go module updates are never auto-merged, whatever they are labelled. postUpdateOptions gomodTidy re-resolves the module graph after Renovate's own edit, and Go's minimal version selection then raises OTHER modules, indirect ones included, to the versions the updated one requires: a branch Renovate calls a patch or a minor can carry a v0 minor bump that Renovate never listed (go-llmflow/gateway#131: go-ndarray v0.18.0 to v0.28.0, go-gfx v0.36.1 to v0.37.0, go-images/jpeg2000 v0.13.8 to v0.14.0, under a title that named none of them). Automerge is decided from what Renovate saw, not from what tidy wrote, so the only rule that cannot be defeated is to merge a gomod branch by hand, after reading its go.mod diff. GitHub Actions and the other managers keep the automerge of the group above.

Never auto-merge the Go toolchain, and never let it ride in somebody else's group. A rule that says automerge:false for one dependency is defeated by grouping, because Renovate decides automerge per BRANCH: go 1.27.0 rode into seven repositories inside a branch called renovate/github-actions, whose other dependency was actions/setup-go. Ungrouped, it gets a branch of its own and this setting governs it. It matters because go1.27.0 miscompiles on loong64 (golang/go#81000, bisected on real hardware to 3fdac6780b): go-gfx/gfx fails that lane and stayed open only because the lane failed, which is the CI gate holding rather than this rule. A repository without such a lane sees nothing.
